title: What is a birdie in golf? One shot under par
description: A birdie means one stroke under par on a hole. See why three shots can be a birdie on one hole but an ordinary par on another, with a simple example.

cover.alt: A golf ball and putter beside a cup and a card reading PAR 4 and SCORE 3 on a putting green

sections.title: One fewer is the good news
sections.html:
A birdie is a score of one stroke under par on a single golf hole. If the hole is a par four and you finish in three strokes, that is a birdie.

The PGA glossary describes par as the score an accomplished player is expected to make. It is the reference number that gives birdie its meaning.

sections.title: Three is not always a birdie
sections.html:
Imagine two friends both finish a hole in three strokes. One played a par four; the other played a par three.

The first has a birdie. The second has made par. Same number of strokes, different result against the hole’s reference score. Cambridge Dictionary makes that one-below-par relationship explicit.

sections.title: The tiny score check
sections.html:
For a birdie, subtract one from the hole’s par: two strokes on a par three, three on a par four, or four on a par five.

Golf gives nearby scores other names, too. In the PGA glossary, a bogey is one over par and an eagle is two under. A birdie sits one stroke below par, without needing a feather in sight.

sections.title: A small number with context
sections.html:
The useful question is not simply how many strokes someone took. Ask what par was for that hole, then compare the two numbers.
